title: The Family I Don't Want Anyone to Know About
paragraphs: "You know... both of you..."
Father looks a bit exasperated.
"By the way, there was also a loop where Kou was well-behaved even without the trauma. That was the loop where I couldn't save Father, and he had to fight hard in Melromarc."
“Ah, so Lord Gaelion is the ‘Wild’ Lord Iwatani… I see—the bandits were a resource.”
“By the way, I heard that when he went hunting bandits again, he referred to it as a ‘harvest’ or something like that.”
“Lord Iwatani!”
“That was my parallel-world self! I didn’t do anything like that!　I’d also appreciate it if Motoyasu-kun wouldn’t say things that cause confusion.”
Father is giving me a dirty look. I was just having a conversation.
“Well… I’d really like to meet that Shield Hero of yours. It seems like we wouldn’t have to go through any trouble with him, since he wouldn’t pry into things unnecessarily.”
“Rasa…”
“Hmm… I do agree that you, Rasa, would probably get along well with that Iwatani over there. I’m sorry if that offended you.”
“It’s fine. So, Kou looks like he’s not afraid of anything—what are you going to do?　Are you going to stir up trouble and make the Shield Hero angry?”
“Ugh… Kou, I’m not scared of Iwatani.”
Hmm, I might have sparked something in Kou’s pride. But there’s a difference between Kou saying he’s “not scared” now and what he meant back then.
“I guess I don’t like being feared either… I don’t think there’s anything good that comes from making me angry, you know?”
“That’s right. Kou, you mustn’t overthink it. Everyone’s praising you for being such a good boy, after all.”
“Hmm… Okay.”
He seemed a little skeptical, but it looks like Kou understood. That settles Kou’s problem!
“Kou, you had such a fun time with Lord Motoyasu today! I’m a little jealous!”
Yuki-chan is looking at Kou with a hint of resentment.
“It was a fun time between two guys.”
“Pick-up line.”
Everyone present—except for Yuki-chan and Sakura-chan—froze solid like ice. Father is looking at me with a troubled expression.
“Hitting on girls… where, and with whom?”
“We went out of the castle to the grasslands and fed the wild Filolials, ran around, and played, right?”
“Well, in a broad sense, I suppose you could call that ‘picking up girls.’ Even though they were wild Filolials… but Kou is a male, so I guess you’re not exactly wrong?”
“It’s a man’s pastime. Encounters are important, after all. That’s how romance begins.”
Memories of nothing but pigs flashed through my mind, but there was no falsehood in how I felt at the time.
“I sort of get what you’re trying to say, but sort of don’t… Come to think of it, Motoyasu-kun is good-looking, and he’s from a world like a dating sim…”
“A dating sim where you hit on people…” Father muttered.
“Next time, let’s go together, Father.”
“No, I’m fine… Besides, given my position…”
And with that, Father gently turned me down. Even though we’re both heroes, is it something he can’t do because of his position? Approaching Filolial-sama is a wonderful thing, isn’t it?

Ah, I see. I understand what Motoyasu—I mean, Father—is thinking now. He’s worried that he’ll be popular with the ladies and I might end up losing out. Back in the first world, when I rushed to join Father, Filolial-sama and the others took a real liking to him, so he’s probably worried that might happen again.
“HAHAHA, no need to worry. It’s all part of the fun—seeing just how many times I get hit on!”
“You don’t get it…”
“I’d rather you didn’t do that too much.”
Yuki-chan looks a little displeased. It’s true—this might not be the best situation for her. But this, too, is part of a man’s worth.

“Yuki-chan, just as a woman’s charm increases when she’s ogled, a man’s worth increases when he picks up women. If you stay naive, you’ll become a hopeless man who lacks poise. It’s a man’s refinement.”
“I see! It’s the refinement of the nobility. As expected of Motoyasu-sama!”
Oh! As expected of Yuki-chan—she really gets it.
“I can’t deny there’s a subtle hint of aristocratic pretension there…”
“True…”
Éclair and Zou say something with a sigh.
“I think I’ll just stay innocent…”
Father mutters under his breath.
“That won’t do, Father! If you stay so naive, Rival will get the better of you!”
That guy is after Father’s virginity! Don’t you think you need to build up some resistance so Father doesn’t get taken advantage of?
“You need the composure to fend off his charges!”
“Ah, yeah, you’re right, Motoyasu-kun. So, is the reason you’re rooting for Elmero-san because he taught Kou something good?”
“That’s right! He was singing happily with Filolial-sama, and he’s a good guy! I want you to get along with him too, Father!”
“Just saying that alone has led us this far off track… It’s exhausting trying to fathom the bizarre mind of the Spear Hero.”
What’s that supposed to mean? The panda’s complaining, but I’m not listening! To begin with, there’s no man as easy to understand as me.
“Yeah, I trust you, Elmero. You’re dependable, and your bodyguard work is solid.”
“I’m flattered.”
“You should get to know him even better.”

He’s a good elephant, after all. I’d like you to suggest that Father play with Filolial-sama together. Lately, Father-in-law has been away—training at Panda’s family home and handling official duties against Rival in Shieldfreeden—so I haven’t been spending quite enough time with Filolial-sama and the others! When I made the suggestion, Panda’s ears perked up, and a smirk spread across his face.
“Sounds good to me! Since we’re at it, let’s pay a visit to Elmero’s family home and announce that the Shield Hero is here.”
His tone was quite brisk, and he was clearly quite excited.
“Lasaaa!”
Zou glared at Panda with a resentful look. What’s the matter? Does he not like it? Since it’s my suggestion, it’s bound to be a good thing.
“Lars-chan? Elmero seems to be kind of against this, though.”
“What’s the matter? Are you saying we can go to my house but not Elmero’s? Isn’t that unfair?”
“Ugh… I can’t argue with that. You really know how to put it, Lars-chan…”
“Hehehe, I want some friends, you see. Let’s go introduce the family we don’t want anyone to know about, Elmero.”
“Uuuugh…”
Zou responds to the panda’s words with a slightly resentful look, as if gritting his back teeth.
“Hmm… By that logic, should I—since I’m treated as a guest general—also show you my family home? Well, I’m a bodyguard, so my role is different from Lord Rasa’s and the others’…”
“Isn’t that right?”
“But, unfortunately, I lost my family in the first wave…”
“Ah…”
Panda seems to understand. After all, Éclair—which is also Big Sister’s hometown—is in ruins. I hear reconstruction has begun in this world by the Queen’s order.
“It’s fine for you. I’m sure it’s been tough for you. But Elmero is a different story. The Shield Hero? I won’t be satisfied until he goes.”
Panda is really pushing for this.
“Sigh… Fine. I guess I did ask Lars-chan to do something reckless out of curiosity. I really did stir up a hornet’s nest.”
“You sure did.”
“But I don’t regret it. Thanks to that, I’ve made quite a few discoveries.”
“I think you should learn your lesson a little, though.”
Father and Panda are having a friendly exchange. At that moment, the representative of the Shusaku race—who had been silently watching the proceedings with a smile—raises his hand.
“Then let’s contact the Puhant family. Is that all right?”
“Um…”
Zou grimaced deeply as he looked at Father and the others, then nodded as if in resignation.
“Yes… I understand. As the Shield Hero of Siltvelt wishes… my family will do our utmost to ensure we don’t cause any trouble.”
I’m starting to get the feeling that something ominous is in the air. For some reason, Zou right now… gives off the same vibe as that thief who was in cahoots with Father in the first world.
“I hope everything goes smoothly…”
Zou said, sounding a bit anxious.
“Elmero, was it Kou’s fault?”
Kou spoke to the subdued Zou with concern. However, Zou smiled at him.
“No, it was something we couldn’t avoid anyway, so this might actually be a good opportunity. So, you don’t need to worry about it.”
“Really?”
“Hmm…?”
“Yes.”
Zou smiled as if to say there was no need for Kou to worry, then brought his hand close to Kou’s head and stopped it there. Kou rubbed his head against that hand, letting himself be stroked.

Come to think of it, I get the impression that Zou interacts with others without using much force. It’s as if he’s trying to project the image of a gentle creature. The Zou I know has a gentle image, but in reality, he was a temperamental animal prone to injuring his keepers. In that regard, Zou is pretty close to his public image.

It also seems accurate that Father is said to be fond of children. He’s concluded that caring for a child would be impossible given Zou’s massive size, so he’s definitely right about that. With a slight sense of unease hanging in the air, we decided to head to Zou’s parents’ house.

So, that’s why we’re heading to Zou’s parents’ house this time. Coming along are Father, three escort knights, me, Yuki-chan, and Kou. Sakura-chan is visiting her Finacée at Father’s request. As expected, Rival is currently busy with miscellaneous tasks for Shieldfreeden. We’ll use a portal to teleport to the nearest location within Siltvelt, then travel by carriage from there.
“Elmero’s family home, huh… It sounds like everything’s on a grand scale.”

“Ah, yes. That’s definitely true. But there are rooms for servants and guests, so we won’t have any trouble staying the night. Actually, if we’re staying overnight, maybe we should go back to the castle?”
Kou is carrying Zou on his back as he runs alongside Father’s carriage, chatting with him. He’s facing slightly backward.
“I wonder if we’ll get to see Elmero’s room?”
“I haven’t been in Lars-chan’s room, so I don’t think so.”
“Tsk!”
The panda is clicking its tongue. What a rude panda.
“No… I don’t think I even have a room there to begin with.”
“Oh, right. You left home to wander around, didn’t you?　So I guess my personal stuff’s been thrown out, too.”
“I didn’t have that much to begin with… Actually, I have more personal stuff in my room at the castle.”
“I’ve been to Elmero’s room—it was huge!”
Kou chimes in here. He’s pretty close with Zou, isn’t he? It’s good to be friends.
“I see.”
“Yeah. Elmero—apparently, his paintings are his treasures. It was a painting of Elmero and Mr. Mouse.”
“Huh, really?”
“Kou wants a painting with everyone in it!”
When Kou smiles, everyone smiles back. That’s quite a good suggestion.
“That sounds wonderful.”
“Mr. Mouse, huh? Is he a Beastman?”
“Super-large Beastmen like Elmero aren’t really good at detailed work. I’ve heard they hire servants and attendants to handle the menial tasks.”

Zou remained silent, gazing into the distance with an expression that made it impossible to read his thoughts. I seem to recall Father from the first world and Ren having expressions like that at times.
“That’s right. In Siltvelt, it’s a common symbiotic relationship where large Beastmen handle combat and physical labor, while small Beastmen and Demi-Humans fill in the gaps.”
“That actually sounds kind of good.”
“Of course… sometimes slaves are used for those tasks. Humans, too…”
“Ah… I see. I heard something similar the other day when I was talking with Her Majesty—that in Melromarc, Demi-Humans and Beastmen also handle heavy labor.”
“That’s right… it’s something Father had hoped to abolish.”
Éclair is joining the conversation. Judging by this exchange… it seems Zou’s family back home is a staunch proponent of slavery.
“Is Elmero’s family like that too?”
“…I doubt they’d actually show the Shield Hero that they’re using human slaves, though.”
“After all, I, Father, and Éclair are all human. Our policy is to hide any negative aspects from Father.”
“I have some strong objections to what Lord Kitamura just said…”
“Ah… yeah. Thinking back on everything that’s happened, I can see why you’d feel that way, but let’s let her continue, Ms. Éclair.”
Éclair seems to be wondering about something—did I say something odd? I see—she’s probably referring to Father’s ability to hold his liquor.
“How rude! It’s true that Father’s tolerance is off the charts, but he’s still human!”
